attributes.name: [GCP Cloud SQL PostgreSQL OTel] Buffer cache hit ratio 95% rolling 30 days
attributes.description: Tracks how efficiently each Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance serves block reads from shared buffers instead of disk. Good events are blocks read from the buffer cache and total events are blocks read from the buffer cache plus disk, both summed from the PostgreSQL-only DELTA metric cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/postgresql/blocks_read_count (per-minute counts by attributes.source, summed across databases). The objective is that 95% of block reads hit the cache over a rolling 30-day window. A falling hit ratio means more disk I/O and slower queries, usually from undersized memory (tier), a working set that outgrows shared_buffers, or inefficient full scans. Caveats: the right ratio depends heavily on the workload. OLTP instances typically stay well above 99%, while analytics or batch-scan workloads can be legitimately lower, so treat 95% as a starting point to tune. 'disk' reads include reads served by the OS page cache, so this measures PostgreSQL buffer efficiency, not physical I/O. The SLO only uses PostgreSQL-only metrics, so no engine marker is needed. It has no data while the instance is stopped or down and does not measure availability; instance-down alerts cover that. Cloud Monitoring data reaches Elasticsearch 3-5 minutes late, so set the SLO sync delay to at least 5m when you create it.
